content:
The minimum is \(2112\).

**Upper bound:** Color the smaller checkerboard color class. A \(65\times65\) board has \(2113\) cells of one parity and \(2112\) of the other. Color the \(2112\) cells of the smaller parity class. Since a knight move always changes parity, no two uncolored cells can be connected by a knight move.

**Lower bound:** We can exhibit \(2112\) disjoint knight-move pairs. Partition the board into:
- a \(60\times60\) square, tiled by \(2\times4\) blocks;
- a \(60\times5\) strip, tiled by \(4\times5\) blocks;
- a \(5\times60\) strip, tiled by \(5\times4\) blocks;
- a \(5\times5\) corner.

Each \(2\times4\) block has a perfect matching, e.g.
\[
(1,1)-(2,3),\ (2,1)-(1,3),\ (1,2)-(2,4),\ (2,2)-(1,4).
\]
A \(5\times4\) block has a perfect matching, and a \(5\times5\) block has a matching of \(12\) pairs leaving one cell. Thus the whole board contains
\[
1800+150+150+12=2112
\]
disjoint knight-move pairs. Any valid coloring must color at least one cell from each such pair, so at least \(2112\) cells are necessary.

\[
\boxed{2112}
\]
